chapter: Joe Martini and Triangle Jazz Blues
title: Joe Martini writes down Leclerc's tunes; Triangle Jazz Blues sales
summary: Leclerc could not read music, so Joe Martini wrote down his numbers. Triangle Jazz Blues sold poorly because it was too hard to play, while Someday You Want Me earned a little.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, how did you get your tunes written down?

Well, I had a fellow, I mentioned it on there just now. Joe Martini did a dead long time ago. And Joe used to take all my numbers down. And the strangest thing about it, when he took this triangle jazz blues down, it would, I notice here it says.
Arranged. I wonder if it has his name there because he took it down.
Yeah. Yeah, let's see. I know it says. Oh, yeah, there it is. Joe Martini. By Joseph M. Martini. Joe Martini.
And he used to take all my stuff down, you see.

And the strange thing about this jazz, I used to go to the Crest stores and play the piano there, you know, and sell these records and play other numbers too, of course. But lots of people couldn't, they couldn't play this triangle jazz. It was too difficult for them. So I didn't make any money. Someday You Want Me. That was on a record. I made a little money out of that. But Triangle Jazz Blues did the cell because people figured it was too difficult. I guess Joe wrote it, Joe just took it down as I wrote it, and I guess it was a little too difficult, you know.
Maybe Betty could run and get the record if the balance is okay now. And someday.
Someday You Want Me and I Won't Want You.
Yeah. Okay. All right. Well, fine. I'd like to see it. I mean, I'd like to hear the record.
And show it to you if we have it.
